main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Choose terrain-conditioned power rather than constant output.

main_argument_chains.claim: Course geometry changes the value of wind and execution precision.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Monitor steep climbs and turns more strictly.

main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use terrain-specific coaching and sensor feedback.

warnings.warning: Equation 3 diverges as T approaches zero, and Equation 4 is introduced as a cap without a calibrated physiologic maximum or a proof that it remains above the chosen P.
Equation 5-6 use alpha, AWC, and Pc with mixed notation (the prose also prints AWS once); coefficient units and fit uncertainty are not closed.
Equation 8 attenuates alpha by a term containing alpha itself; for sufficiently large Wex the coefficient can become negative, yet no lower bound or reset rule is given.
Equation 9-11 are singular when relative velocity is zero and depend on an unstated wind-direction convention; lateral wind components are discarded by projection.
Equation 13 writes finite differences for kinetic energy as m v Delta-v/Delta-t without a clear evaluation point, then Equation 14 mixes vi and v conventions.
Equation 15 contains a/v and therefore requires v>0; the paper gives no coefficient derivation, initialization, numerical solver, step tolerance, or failure handling.
Equation 21's fourth-root safe-speed expression has unresolved dimensions and an unclear sign inside the radicand; invalid radicands are not handled.
Equation 22 constrains an integral of dt as total energy and names Elim without a power integrand or value, so the total-energy constraint is not operationally closed.
The SA algorithm omits initial and terminal temperatures, cooling factor values, proposal variance, iteration count, random seed, and a reproducible stopping tolerance.
Equation 24 writes epsilon as both a deviation scale and a normal-distribution parameter, leaving variance versus standard deviation ambiguous.
Equations 25-26 sequentially clamp each section but do not show that the repair preserves the energy state, total-energy constraint, or the nominal target comparison.
The team model assumes identical riders, constant safe spacing, instantaneous formation changes, and 720 or 24 permutations without calibrating drafting coefficients or collision dynamics.
The complex team objective optimizes drop point, power, and ordering but reports no numerical drop point, objective value, convergence trace, fourth-finisher tie rule, or individual fatigue state.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Figure 1 workflow: routes physiology through power curve, course dynamics, sensitivity, team extension, and guidance.
Figure 2 topographic map: supplies the Olympic course image and the pixel-to-node preprocessing premise.
Table 1 notation: anchors power, energy, velocity, geometry, and friction symbols with units.
Figure 3 fitted power curve: visualizes the calibrated decreasing power-duration relation.
Figure 4 rider profiles: compares time-trial specialist, sprinter, and female cyclist curves.
Figure 5 force analysis: displays driving, aerodynamic, normal, friction, gravity, and slope terms.
Figure 6 sharp-turn analysis: maps tangent and normal friction to curvature radius.
Figure 7 single disturbance: shows stochastic proposal, feasibility test, and accept/reject loop.
Figure 8 SA flow chart: records initialization, perturbation, objective comparison, cooling, and output.
Figure 9 smoothed course-1 power: translates noisy SA output into a readable terrain strategy.
Figure 10 course-1 AWC and velocity panels: links internal energy state to speed distribution.
Figure 11 course-1 optimization process: supplies an internal search-performance trace.
Figure 12 course-2 power distribution: enables cross-course comparison.
Figure 13 self-designed route: exposes spline-generated geometry used in the third scenario.
Figure 14 course-3 power distribution: shows the intermediate terrain-conditioned strategy.
Figure 15 wind-speed sensitivity: paired course panels distinguish weak and strong response.
Figure 16 wind-direction sensitivity: paired directional scatter supports the course-orientation claim.
Figure 17 whole-model deviation sensitivity: plots bias against disturbance scale.
Figure 18 local sensitivity/elevation: aligns critical road sections with topography.
Figure 19 guidance profiles: translates rider-type differences for the Directeur Sportif.
Figure 20 guidance power distribution: converts the optimized course trace into an operational display.
